steps.title: Announcement of Elections
steps.description: The Election Commission of India (ECI) announces the election schedule, including dates for nominations, scrutiny, withdrawal, and polling. The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) comes into immediate effect.
steps.description_beginner: The Election Commission tells everyone when the election will happen. From this moment, parties must follow strict rules.
steps.did_you_know: India's general election is the largest democratic exercise in the world, involving over 900 million eligible voters.

steps.title: Nomination of Candidates
steps.description: Prospective candidates file nomination papers with the Returning Officer. Each must submit a security deposit and an affidavit disclosing criminal records, assets, and educational qualifications.
steps.description_beginner: People who want to run for office fill out paperwork and pay a deposit. They must share info about their background and money.
steps.did_you_know: In the 2024 general election, over 8,000 candidates filed nominations across 543 constituencies.

steps.title: Scrutiny of Nominations
steps.description: The Returning Officer examines all nomination papers for completeness and validity. Papers with errors or disqualifying conditions are rejected.
steps.description_beginner: Officials check if all the paperwork is correct. If someone made a mistake or is not allowed to run, their application is rejected.
steps.did_you_know: A candidate can be disqualified for failing to submit their election expenditure account within 30 days of the result.

steps.title: Withdrawal of Candidature
steps.description: Candidates may voluntarily withdraw their nomination before the deadline, often due to party negotiations or strategic alliances.
steps.description_beginner: Some candidates decide to drop out before the deadline, often when parties make deals to support each other.
steps.did_you_know: Strategic withdrawals are key to coalition politics in India — parties often trade constituencies to maximize seats.

steps.title: Campaign Period
steps.description: Political parties campaign through rallies, advertisements, door-to-door canvassing, and social media. The ECI monitors expenditure and enforces the Model Code of Conduct.
steps.description_beginner: Candidates try to win votes by holding meetings, putting up ads, and talking to people. There are rules about how much they can spend.
steps.did_you_know: The campaign expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate is 95 lakh rupees in most states.

steps.title: Polling Day
steps.description: Voters cast ballots at designated polling stations using Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) paired with VVPAT units. Security forces and observers ensure a free and fair process.
steps.description_beginner: This is the day people vote! They go to a voting center and press a button on a machine to pick their favorite candidate.
steps.did_you_know: India conducts elections in multiple phases (7 in 2024) to allow security forces to be redeployed across the country.

steps.title: Counting of Votes
steps.description: Sealed EVMs are transported to counting centers. On counting day, votes are tallied electronically, and mandatory VVPAT slip verification is conducted for random samples.
steps.description_beginner: After voting ends, officials open the voting machines and add up all the votes. They check paper slips from some machines too.
steps.did_you_know: VVPAT slips from 5 randomly selected polling stations per constituency are matched against EVM counts as a mandatory audit.

steps.title: Declaration of Results
steps.description: The Returning Officer declares winning candidates. The party or coalition with a majority (272 of 543 seats) is invited to form the government. Results are published in real time.
steps.description_beginner: The winners are announced! The party that wins the most seats gets to form the government. Results are shared live online.
steps.did_you_know: The ECI's result portal receives over 100 million page views on counting day.

phases.name: Pre-Election Phase
phases.description: Voter registration drives, constituency delimitation, and preparation of electoral rolls.

phases.name: Campaign Phase
phases.description: Active campaigning, rallies, media outreach, and enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct.

phases.name: Voting Phase
phases.description: Polling day operations, EVM deployment, and voter turnout monitoring.

phases.name: Post-Election Phase
phases.description: Vote counting, result declaration, government formation, and election petitions.

roles.name: Election Commission of India
roles.description: The autonomous constitutional body responsible for administering all election processes in India.

roles.name: Chief Election Commissioner
roles.description: The head of the Election Commission who presides over all decisions.

roles.name: Returning Officer
roles.description: Official appointed for each constituency to manage the election process locally.

roles.name: Booth Level Officer
roles.description: Local official responsible for maintaining voter lists and assisting voters.

roles.name: Election Observer
roles.description: Independent official deputed by ECI to monitor election proceedings.

key_terms.definition: A standalone electronic device used to record votes in Indian elections.
A printer attached to the EVM that produces a paper slip for vote verification.
Guidelines issued by ECI to regulate political parties and candidates during elections.
An option on the EVM that allows voters to reject all candidates.
Photo ID card issued by ECI to all registered voters.
The process of redrawing electoral constituency boundaries based on census data.
Targeted drives to register newly eligible or previously missed voters.
A ballot paper sent by mail to voters who cannot visit a polling station.

quiz.question: Which body conducts general elections in India?
quiz.explanation: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes.

quiz.question: What does EVM stand for?
quiz.explanation: EVM stands for Electronic Voting Machine, used to cast and record votes.

quiz.question: What comes into effect when elections are announced?
quiz.explanation: The Model Code of Conduct regulates behavior of parties and candidates from the date of announcement.

quiz.question: How many seats are in the Lok Sabha?
quiz.explanation: The Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats. A party needs 272 for a majority.

quiz.question: What is NOTA?
options: None Of The Above option on EVM
quiz.explanation: NOTA allows voters to reject all candidates without spoiling their ballot. Introduced in 2013.

quiz.question: What does VVPAT verify?
options: The vote cast by the voter
quiz.explanation: VVPAT produces a paper slip showing the selected candidate, allowing vote confirmation.

quiz.question: Who accepts nomination papers?
quiz.explanation: The Returning Officer manages elections at constituency level, including accepting nominations.

quiz.question: What is the minimum voting age in India?
quiz.explanation: The minimum voting age is 18 years, per the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988.

quiz.question: How many phases were in the 2024 election?
quiz.explanation: The 2024 election was conducted in 7 phases for security force redeployment.

quiz.question: What is delimitation?
quiz.explanation: Delimitation is redrawing electoral boundaries based on census data for equal representation.
